mainTopic: Keeping the calendar far from בית דין: two-day יום טוב, doubtful יום כיפור, leap years, and a moon-sign for burning חמץ
overview: This amud is about how people far from בית דין kept the calendar. It opens by finishing an earlier point: two short months in a row would become well known. לוי came to בבל and saw people eating on the day that was really יום כיפור in ארץ ישראל. He would not testify, though, because he had not personally heard בית דין declare the month. רבי יוחנן ruled that places the ניסן messengers reach, but the תשרי messengers do not, must keep two days of פסח as a גזירה. He was upset when two of his students did not enforce it. Then come stories of doubt about יום כיפור: רבא fasted two days, and רב נחמן got news right at the end of his fast that he had to fast again. רב הונא בר אבין taught that a year is made a leap year if winter would last past the 16th of ניסן, based on "שמור את חדש האביב". Finally, רב נחמן gave sailors a moon-sign for burning חמץ, and the גמרא explains why it works on the 14th at sea.

steps.title: Two short months in a row would be well known
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers an earlier worry: if two months in a row were made חסר (29 days), everyone would hear about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two short months in a row get publicized.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering an earlier question. It says there is no need to worry about two months in a row both being made short, because something that unusual becomes widely known.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a far-away community can count on a normal pattern of months. If בית דין ever made two months in a row חסר, that would be so unusual that word would spread. So people do not have to worry that it happened without their knowing.

keyTerms.meaning: they have a 'voice', meaning they become publicly known

phrases.english: Two months that are made short
phrases.notes: A short month has 29 days instead of 30. Here it means two of them in a row.

phrases.english: have a 'voice' to them, so it becomes known.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּרֵי יַרְחֵי חַסִּירֵי קָלָא אִית לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question from the end of the previous section of the דף.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual reality: an unusual calendar change would be well publicized.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have worried that two months in a row were made short, and that far-away communities would not know.
steps.terutzMaskana: Such a change becomes widely known, so there is no need to worry about it.

steps.title: לוי sees the Babylonians eating on the real יום כיפור
steps.stepSummary: לוי came to בבל on what they counted as the 11th of תשרי. He remarked that they were eating on the day that was יום כיפור in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי came to בבל on the eleventh of תשרי. He said: How tasty is the food of the Babylonians on the great day of the West (ארץ ישראל)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story. לוי arrives in בבל and notices that the local calendar is one day ahead of the calendar in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ארץ ישראל, אלול had been made a full month, so that day was really the 10th of תשרי, which is יום כיפור. בבל counted it as the 11th, so people there were eating. לוי's comment about how tasty their food is was a pointed way of saying they were eating on יום כיפור.

phrases.english: Levi arrived in Babylonia
on the eleventh of Tishrei.
phrases.notes: This was the 11th by the Babylonian count. In ארץ ישראל it was only the 10th.

phrases.english: He said: How tasty is the dish of the Babylonians
on the great day of the West!
phrases.notes: 'The great day' is יום כיפור, and 'the West' is ארץ ישראל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story showing that the calendar in בבל could be off from the one in ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A story showing that בבל was one day off from ארץ ישראל on יום כיפור.

steps.title: לוי refuses to testify
steps.stepSummary: The Babylonians asked לוי to testify so they could change their day. He refused, because he had not personally heard בית דין declare the month 'מקודש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Testify! He said to them: I did not hear from the mouth of בית דין 'It is sanctified.'
steps.whatsHappening: The people of בבל ask לוי to give formal testimony so they can fix their calendar. He says no, because he did not hear it from בית דין himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לוי knew that אלול had been made full, but his knowledge was secondhand. Testimony that can change a community's calendar has to come from someone who personally heard בית דין's declaration. Without that, the community keeps its usual count.

keyTerms.meaning: the court that declares the new month
'It is sanctified', the court's declaration of the new month

steps.confusionAlert: לוי was not unsure about the date. He knew it. He refused only because formal testimony needs firsthand hearing of בית דין, not just knowledge.

phrases.english: They said to him: Testify!
He said to them: I did not hear
from the mouth of the court 'It is sanctified.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the לוי story with the community's request and his answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Testimony that changes the calendar needs someone who personally heard בית דין say 'מקודש'.
steps.whatToRemember: לוי knew the true date, but without firsthand hearing of בית דין he could not testify, so בבל kept its own count.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's decree: keep two days of פסח where the תשרי messengers don't reach
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן announced that any place reached by the ניסן messengers but not the תשרי messengers must keep two days of פסח. This is a גזירה because of תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן proclaimed: Anywhere the messengers of ניסן reach, but the messengers of תשרי do not reach, should keep two days. This is a גזירה on ניסן because of תשרי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן makes a public ruling. Some places hear about ניסן in time, but those same places must still keep two days of פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In תשרי the messengers could not travel on ראש השנה or יום כיפור, so they got less far than in ניסן. Places in between would know the right date for פסח, but not for סוכות. רבי יוחנן required two days of פסח there anyway, so people would not get used to one day and then keep only one day of סוכות too.

keyTerms.meaning: the messengers sent by בית דין to announce the month
a rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
because of, out of concern for

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that keeping two days of יום טוב is sometimes a safeguard, even in places that actually know the right date.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan proclaimed:
Anywhere that the messengers of Nisan reach,
but the messengers of Tishrei do not reach,
let them keep two days.
It is a decree on Nisan because of Tishrei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the לוי story to a formal ruling about how far-away places keep יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Places reached in ניסן but not in תשרי keep two days of פסח, as a גזירה because of תשרי.

steps.title: Two students see a town keeping one day and stay silent
steps.stepSummary: רבי אייבו בר נגרי and רבי חייא בר אבא came to a place in the in-between zone. The people there kept only one day, and the students said nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אייבו בר נגרי and רבי חייא בר אבא came to a certain place that the ניסן messengers reached but the תשרי messengers did not. The people kept one day, and the students did not say anything to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that sets up רבי יוחנן's reaction in the next step. Two of his students saw people breaking his decree and did not correct them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This town is exactly the kind of place רבי יוחנן's decree was about. The people kept only one day of פסח, against the גזירה. The point of the story is that the students stayed silent.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אַיְיבוּ בַּר נַגָּרֵי וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: Rabbi Aivu bar Naggarei and Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba
arrived at a certain place
that the messengers of Nisan would reach
but the messengers of Tishrei would not reach,
and they were keeping one day,
phrases.notes: 'They' here means the local people, keeping one day of פסח.

phrases.english: and they did not say anything at all to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַיְיבוּ בַּר נַגָּרֵי וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אִיקְּלַעוּ לְהָהוּא אַתְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי יוחנן's decree to a real case where it was not followed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story setup: a town in the in-between zone kept one day, and the students did not protest.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן gets upset and repeats his decree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן heard what happened and was upset. He reminded his students of his ruling that such places must keep two days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן heard and became upset. He said to them: Didn't I tell you that wherever the ניסן messengers reach but the תשרי messengers do not, they should keep two days, as a גזירה on ניסן because of תשרי?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן scolds his students for not correcting the town. He repeats his decree word for word to show it was serious and they should have spoken up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא repeats the exact wording of the decree from step 4 on purpose. This time it is a rebuke. It shows that the גזירה is binding, and that a student who sees people breaking it has to say something.

keyTerms.meaning: became upset, was strict about it

steps.whatToRemember: In places the תשרי messengers can't reach, two days of פסח must be kept, even though they know the right date for ניסן. רבי יוחנן insisted this decree be enforced.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan heard and became upset.
He said to them: Did I not tell you
that wherever the messengers of Nisan reach
but the messengers of Tishrei do not reach
they should keep two days,
as a decree on Nisan because of Tishrei!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוחנן reacts to the students' silence in step 5 by restating his decree from step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן's גזירה is binding: places reached in ניסן but not in תשרי must keep two days of פסח, and this must be enforced.

steps.title: רבא fasted two days of יום כיפור
steps.stepSummary: רבא used to fast for two days of יום כיפור because he was unsure of the date, and once the second day turned out to be the real יום כיפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא used to fast for two days. One time it turned out that he was right.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about רבא, who fasted two days of יום כיפור in case the people in בבל had the date wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If בית דין made אלול a 30-day month, יום כיפור would fall one day later than בבל assumed, just like in לוי's story from step 2. רבא covered himself by fasting both days, and one year that is exactly what happened.

keyTerms.meaning: Used to do it, was in the habit
It turned out like him, he was proven right

steps.confusionAlert: רבא did not hold that יום כיפור is always two days. He fasted two days only because he was not sure which day was the real one.

phrases.english: Rava was accustomed
to sit in a fast for two days.
phrases.notes: He means the fast of יום כיפור, kept on two days in case אלול had 30 days.

phrases.english: One time it turned out to be like him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא הֲוָה רְגִיל דַּהֲוָה יָתֵיב בְּתַעֲנִיתָא תְּרֵי יוֹמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another story showing how unsure בבל was about the dates set in ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of doubt about the date, רבא fasted two days of יום כיפור, and one year the second day was the real one.

steps.title: רב נחמן hears that יום כיפור is tomorrow
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן fasted a full יום כיפור. At night a man arrived and told him that tomorrow is יום כיפור in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן fasted the whole day of יום כיפור. In the evening a man came and told him: tomorrow is the great day in the West.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second story: רב נחמן finished his fast and then got news that יום כיפור was really the next day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבא, רב נחמן fasted only one day. The news arrived right at the end of his fast, so he would now have to fast a second day in a row. The next step shows how he reacted.

keyTerms.meaning: The great day, meaning יום כיפור

phrases.english: Rav Nachman sat in a fast
the whole day of Yom Kippur.
In the evening a certain man came

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לִמְחַר יוֹמָא רַבָּה בְּמַעְרְבָא.
phrases.english: and said to him: Tomorrow is the great day in the West.
phrases.notes: "The West" is ארץ ישראל, which is west of בבל.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן יְתֵיב בְּתַעֲנִיתָא כּוּלֵּיהּ יוֹמֵי דְּכִיפּוּרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story on the same theme. This time the person fasted only one day, and the news came at the very end of his fast, so he now had to fast a second day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן learned after his fast that יום כיפור in ארץ ישראל was the next day.

steps.title: רב נחמן's pained reaction
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks the man where he is from. He answers דמהריא, and רב נחמן makes a play on the name, meaning this news will be painful. He quotes a פסוק about pursuers being too quick.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן asked: Where are you from? He said: From דמהריא. רב נחמן said: Blood will be his end. And he quoted about him: "Our pursuers were swift."
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with רב נחמן reacting to the bad news: now he must fast a second day in a row.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name דמהריא sounds like "דם", blood, so רב נחמן says the end will be "blood," meaning the suffering of a second fast. The פסוק "our pursuers were swift" fits because if the man had come a bit later, they would already have eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: דמהריא, the name of a place
He read a פסוק about him

steps.confusionAlert: "Blood will be his end" is wordplay on the town's name, דמהריא, which sounds like "דם". It shows how painful the news of a second fast in a row was.

phrases.english: He said to him: Where are you from?
He said to him: From Damihareya.
He said to him: Blood will be his end.
phrases.notes: A play on the town's name: "דמהריא" sounds like "דם", blood.

phrases.english: He read about him: "Our pursuers were swift."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the רב נחמן story with his reaction to the news.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן accepted the news and saw the second fast as a painful burden that came just in time.

steps.title: When to add a leap month
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר אבין tells רבא: if winter (the תקופה of טבת) would last until the 16th of ניסן, make the year a leap year, and do not worry about it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר אבין sent this to רבא: When you see that the season of טבת stretches until the 16th of ניסן, add a month to that year, and don't worry about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new calendar topic: a rule for when to make a leap year (עיבור שנה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The year should be made longer if spring would otherwise start after the 16th of ניסן. רב הונא בר אבין says this reason is enough by itself, so רבא does not need any other reason. The next step gives the פסוק behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: The season of טבת, the winter season
Make it a leap year, add a month

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key rule for keeping the Jewish calendar in line with the seasons, so that פסח always falls in spring.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בַּר אָבִין לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Avin sent to Rava:
When you see that the season of Tevet extends
phrases.notes: The season of טבת means winter. The point is that spring would only begin late.

phrases.english: until the sixteenth of Nisan,
make that year a leap year
and don't worry about it,
phrases.notes: He means: you don't need any other reason to add the month.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַח לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בַּר אָבִין לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new calendar topic. It moves from doubts about the day of the month to the rules for adding a leap month.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If winter would last past the 16th of ניסן, the year is made a leap year, and this reason alone is enough.

steps.title: The verse behind the leap-year rule
steps.stepSummary: The source is "שמור את חדש האביב": make sure the spring of the season falls in ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: "Guard the month of spring." This means: guard the spring of the season so that it falls in the month of ניסן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the פסוק that supports רב הונא בר אבין's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה commands us to "guard" spring, meaning we must make sure spring and ניסן line up. If spring would come too late, adding a month moves ניסן later so that it matches the spring season.

keyTerms.meaning: The season, here the start of spring

steps.whatToRemember: A leap month is added whenever spring would otherwise begin after the 16th of ניסן, because the תורה says to make sure spring falls in ניסן.

phrases.english: as it is written: "Guard the month of spring,"
guard the spring of the season
so that it will be in the month of Nisan.
phrases.notes: "חֹדֶשׁ" also means "new." So spring should come in the new part of ניסן, before פסח.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the rule in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a year is made a leap year if winter would last until the 16th of ניסן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 16:1, "שמור את חדש האביב", read as a command to make sure spring falls in ניסן.

steps.title: רב נחמן gives sailors a moon-sign for burning חמץ
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן tells sea travelers: since you won't know when the month began, burn your חמץ when you see the moon shining all night until daybreak.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to sailors: You won't know when the month was set. So when you see the moon lasting the whole night until daybreak, burn your חמץ.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives practical advice to sailors who are out of touch with the בית דין's announcement of ראש חודש ניסן. He tells them to use the full moon as their sign for ביעור חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the earlier steps about people unsure of the date, like רבא fasting two days. The month is set by the בית דין, so someone far away cannot count the days. The moon itself becomes a natural calendar: when it is visible from sunset until sunrise, it is the middle of the month.

keyTerms.meaning: The setting of the month, when the בית דין fixes the first day
Lasts until daybreak, completes its course at sunrise

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to them,
to those sea travelers:
You, who will not know
when the month was set,
when you see the moon
that lasts until daybreak,
phrases.notes: He means the moon stays up the whole night, from sunset until sunrise, which happens at full moon.

phrases.english: burn the leaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב נַחְמָן לְהָנְהוּ נָחוֹתֵי יַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of people uncertain of the calendar date, now applied to ביעור חמץ.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sailors who do not know the date should burn their חמץ when the moon is visible all night until daybreak.

steps.title: The full moon comes on the 15th, but חמץ is burned on the 14th
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when the moon lasts until daybreak, answers the 15th, and objects that חמץ must be burned already on the 14th.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does the moon last until daybreak? On the 15th. But we burn חמץ from the 14th!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן's sign. If the moon only stays up all night on the 15th, the sailors would burn their חמץ a day too late.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The short question-and-answer 'when does it complete? on the 15th' sets up the problem. By the 15th it is already פסח, and חמץ must be gone by the 14th. So the sign seems to give the wrong day.

phrases.english: When does it last until daybreak?
On the fifteenth.
But we burn it from the fourteenth!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַת מַשְׁלֵים בַּחֲמֵיסַר וְהָא אֲנַן מֵאַרְבֵּיסַר מְבַעֲרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the timing of רב נחמן's sign.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's instruction to burn חמץ when the moon lasts until daybreak.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The moon lasts all night only on the 15th, but ביעור חמץ must happen on the 14th, so the sign would be one day late.

steps.title: At sea the moon already looks full on the 14th
steps.stepSummary: For sailors, who see an open horizon, the moon already appears to last until daybreak on the 14th.
steps.simpleTranslation: For them, since the world is wide open to them, the moon already lasts until daybreak from the 14th.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that sailors see the whole horizon. So for them the moon already seems to stay up all night on the 14th, and the sign gives the right day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On land, hills and buildings block the view near sunrise and sunset. At sea nothing blocks it, so the moon can be seen all night already on the 14th. רב נחמן's sign was made for sailors and fits them exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: The world is revealed to them, the horizon is open and clear

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's moon-sign works for sailors because the open horizon at sea lets them see the moon all night already on the 14th, the day of ביעור חמץ.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say the moon is different at sea. It says the view is clearer there, so the all-night moon can be seen one day earlier.

phrases.english: For them, to whom the world is revealed,
phrases.notes: At sea nothing blocks the horizon, so they can see the moon right down to the edge.

phrases.english: it already lasts until daybreak from the fourteenth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by limiting the sign to sailors' viewing conditions.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the sailors' situation differs from people on land.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The moon is seen lasting all night only on the 15th, so the sign comes too late.
steps.terutzMaskana: At sea, with an open horizon, the moon is seen lasting all night already on the 14th, so the sign is correct for sailors.
